description: Single sign-on, MFA, privileged access, and account lifecycle for every workforce and client-facing system
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Every process signs in through the identity platform (SYS-04); an outage stops all work in 64 offices and remote; identity changes must not be lost (RPO 15 min, replicated directory)
manual_workaround: Sealed break-glass accounts per critical platform; secondary region for the identity service
dependent_third_parties: Identity platform vendor (SaaS components); Cloud provider A
dependent_people_or_facilities: Identity and Access Management team; SOC
quantified_impact_basis: All work stops: about $19.0 million of average daily receipts at risk (higher in peak season); counted once here, not added to other rows
acquired_firm_dependency: AF-05 and AF-06 use their own directories (not affected by an outage, but not protected by it either)
single_points_of_failure: Single identity platform (by design; standby region)

business_process: Individual and private client tax return preparation and review
description: Preparers enter and review Form 1040 series returns for about 700,000 individual consumers; partners sign high-net-worth returns
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Peak-season values (January 15 to April 15; September 1 to October 15): a lost day near a deadline means late returns and penalty reimbursements; the tax application database replicates hourly (RPO 1 h)
manual_workaround: File extensions (Form 4868) early for unfinished clients; prioritize by deadline; move work between offices and to remote staff
dependent_third_parties: Tax software vendor; Cloud provider A; DMS vendor
dependent_people_or_facilities: About 4,100 tax preparers and reviewers; seasonal staff; all offices or remote
quantified_impact_basis: About 40% of peak tax production lost per day of outage (about $6.2 million) plus about $1.3 million of overtime and expected penalty reimbursements
acquired_firm_dependency: AF-05 and AF-06 prepare returns on their own tax software (see BP-17)
single_points_of_failure: Single tax software instance (hosted on Cloud provider A)

description: Release signed returns and extensions through the tax software vendor's transmitter; track IRS and state acknowledgments and rejects
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Returns and extensions must be transmitted by the deadline; acknowledgments prove timely filing; the vendor contract RTO for the transmitter is 12 h, which misses the 8 h BIA RTO in peak season (DEP-01)
manual_workaround: Paper filing with proof of mailing for extensions as a last resort; IRS Free File is not available to preparers, so there is no second transmitter today (gap 7)
dependent_third_parties: Tax software vendor (Authorized IRS e-file transmitter); IRS and state e-file systems
dependent_people_or_facilities: e-file operations team; Responsible Officials for 30 EFINs
quantified_impact_basis: Rework, missed deadlines on about 9,000 returns a peak day, and expected penalty reimbursements
acquired_firm_dependency: AF-05 and AF-06 transmit under their own EFINs through a different vendor

business_process: Client document intake and data extraction
description: Receive source documents through the portal, email, and mail; scan, index, and file to the DMS; AI extraction fills return input fields (AI-001)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Preparers stall without documents; clients keep originals so lost scans can be re-collected; portal uploads replicate to the standby region (RPO 4 h for the extraction queue)
manual_workaround: Preparers key data manually from source images; extraction turned off; portal uploads read directly
dependent_systems: SYS-02; SYS-03; AI extraction pipeline; SYS-10 printer-scanners
dependent_third_parties: Cloud provider A; DMS vendor; AI model provider (AI-001 sub-processor)
dependent_people_or_facilities: Intake and scanning teams in 12 processing hubs
quantified_impact_basis: About 30,000 documents a peak day delayed; manual keying costs about $1.1 million a day plus deadline slippage
single_points_of_failure: AI model provider for extraction (manual fallback exists)

description: Clients sign Forms 8879, 8878, engagement letters, and IRC 7216 consents and download returns in the portal
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: The ERO may not transmit until the taxpayer signs Form 8879 (IRS Pub. 1345); IRC 7216 consents must be signed before the disclosure (301.7216-3(b)(1)); identity verification service required for e-signature
manual_workaround: Wet-signature Forms 8879 and consents by courier or office visit; paper returns
dependent_third_parties: Cloud provider A; identity verification service for e-signature
quantified_impact_basis: Delayed transmissions and courier costs for about 7,000 signatures a peak day
single_points_of_failure: Single identity verification service for e-signature (DEP-10)

business_process: Business, trust, and international tax compliance
description: Corporate, partnership, trust, exempt-organization, and international returns; state and local filings
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Deadlines on March 15, April 15, September 15, and October 15; extensions are routine but penalties for late partnership returns accrue per partner per month; offshore provider drafts some returns (DEP-12)
manual_workaround: File extensions for every unfinished entity; shift offshore work back on-shore
dependent_third_parties: Tax software vendor; offshore tax outsourcing provider; Cloud provider A
quantified_impact_basis: About 35% of business tax production lost per peak day plus extension rework
acquired_firm_dependency: AF-05 and AF-06 prepare their business returns locally

business_process: Tax compliance outsourcing and global mobility (SL-2)
description: Managed tax compliance for about 380 corporate clients through the corporate client tax portal, including returns for about 38,000 global mobility assignees
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Contract service levels promise portal availability of 99.5% and 24-hour response; assignees' personal data is covered by privacy commitments (P09 SL-2)
manual_workaround: Secure file exchange through the DMS; extensions; client calls
dependent_third_parties: Cloud provider A; tax software vendor
quantified_impact_basis: Service credits and labor for about 380 corporate clients; reputational harm with multinational clients
single_points_of_failure: Corporate tax portal runs in one primary region with warm standby

description: Outsourced bookkeeping, close, bill pay, and payroll for about 3,100 client businesses (about 410,000 client employees)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Payroll must be funded and paid on the pay date; payroll tax deposits have fixed deadlines; SOC 1 and SOC 2 commitments to clients (P09)
manual_workaround: Repeat the prior payroll for salaried employees; manual ACH file through the bank portal; client pays vendors directly
dependent_third_parties: Cloud provider B; accounting SaaS provider; ACH originating bank; payroll tax filing service
quantified_impact_basis: About 14,000 paychecks a day at risk on peak pay dates; penalty and late-payment exposure for clients; service credits

description: Plan, perform, and document audits and reviews in the audit platform; about 140 SEC issuer audits
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Issuer clients' annual report deadlines cluster from late February to March; audit documentation must be preserved; workpapers hold PHI for health care clients
manual_workaround: Work offline in synchronized local engagement files; reschedule non-urgent fieldwork
dependent_third_parties: Audit software vendor; Cloud provider B
quantified_impact_basis: About 70% of assurance production per day in the January to March peak (about $5.7 million average daily assurance receipts)

description: Email, phones, portal messaging, and contact center for clients and taxing authorities
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Deadline questions and document requests peak in season; email is also the business email compromise attack path (P08); the email vendor retains mailbox data
manual_workaround: Website and portal notices; phone tree; temporary clean mailboxes after a compromise
dependent_people_or_facilities: Contact center (about 220 agents); all client-facing staff
quantified_impact_basis: Lost productivity and missed client deadlines; higher in peak season

description: Risk, transaction, health care, and government services consulting, including data rooms with PHI and Federal Contract Information
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Few regulatory deadlines; transaction work has deal deadlines; FCI and PHI stores must stay protected during recovery
manual_workaround: Reschedule; work from local synchronized files
quantified_impact_basis: About 40% of daily advisory receipts deferred

description: SOC 1 and SOC 2 examinations for about 610 service organization clients a year
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Report dates are set by client commitments, usually with some slack
manual_workaround: Reschedule fieldwork; work from local files
quantified_impact_basis: About 35% of daily SOC receipts deferred

business_process: IRS and state notice response and representation
description: Respond to taxing authority notices and examinations within notice deadlines
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Most notices allow 30 days or more; deadlines can often be extended by phone
manual_workaround: Call the agency for more time; work from paper copies

description: Check independence and conflicts before accepting attest and non-attest engagements
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: An attest engagement accepted without an independence check is a professional standards violation; new engagements can wait a few days
manual_workaround: Manual independence checks by the Office of General Counsel for urgent engagements
dependent_people_or_facilities: Office of General Counsel; independence team

business_process: Time, billing, collections, and firm finance
description: Time capture, invoicing, collections, and partner distributions
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Cash peaks in April and October; invoices can be delayed a few days
manual_workaround: Manual invoices for large clients; pay by wire or check

business_process: Firm payroll, HR, and seasonal onboarding
description: Firm payroll, onboarding of about 1,500 seasonal staff in January, terminations (which drive access removal)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Payroll runs biweekly; seasonal onboarding in January; terminations feed identity governance
manual_workaround: Repeat the prior payroll; manual onboarding and termination checklist
dependent_third_parties: HR and payroll SaaS vendor; background screening provider
quantified_impact_basis: Overtime and penalty exposure on missed payroll

business_process: Tax operations at acquired firms AF-05 and AF-06
description: Tax preparation, e-file, and email at two acquired firms still on legacy systems until integration
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Their own tax software and EFINs; nightly backups only (real RPO 24 h); their managed service providers' contracts state a 24-hour restore
manual_workaround: Move AF preparers onto the enterprise tax platform early for urgent returns; file extensions
dependent_systems: AF-05 and AF-06 email tenants, tax software, and file servers
dependent_third_parties: AF-05 and AF-06 managed service providers; their tax software vendor
dependent_people_or_facilities: About 410 staff at AF-05 and AF-06
quantified_impact_basis: About 4% of tax production; deadline exposure for their clients
